newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Feb/March trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Feb/March trade data.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' reactions to data showing Britain's trade deficit with the rest of the world was 758 million stg in February and the non-EU trade deficit in March was 606 million:
"This provides tentative evidence that the appreciation in the currency is having some effect on export volumes."

"Non-EU numbers are worse than we expected but in line with the market consensus. Export volumes are well down in March in the non-EU figures excluding oil and erratics. We had a drop in export volumes in the February global numbers as well. So it's tentative evidence that the behaviour of the currency is having some effect on exports but the data are very erratic on a month to month basis and it's far from convincing evidence."

"The headline figures are better than expected, if anything suggesting that the deficit is actually narrowing. So no immediate signs that sterling's appreciation is biting into competitiveness and export voluems growth as yet. But the worst definitely seems to be yet to come -- all the surveys are pointing to fairly sharp drops in export orders."

"UK trade data came out broadly as had been expected but there was some evidence of a softening in exports which may be a small negative for the pound...If the deterioration in exports continues, there could be some widening in the trade position later in the year -- particularly as import values are being depressed by the impact of the rise in the pound. The numbers may be a small negative for the pound and a small positive for short sterling, but are probably close enough to expectations to have limited impact.
